title: Checkorca parser pack
description: A parser pack turns one kind of alert mail into results (Interfaces chapter of the dev-work-plan, Pack YAML; docs/parsers.md explains every key). The loader (app/parsers/loader.py) also compiles every regex, checks that an extract regex has exactly one named group, that a field gives regex or literal, that a literal is plain text, that a time format reads back what it writes and that a verified pack has fixtures of at least 3 classes. Name patterns end in (?!\n) because Python reads $ as the end or a final line break.

id.description: Unique pack id; the file name of a built-in pack.

version.description: Raised by one for every change of the pack.

status.description: verified: checked against fixtures of at least 3 classes; unverified-synthetic: written from documentation with synthetic fixtures only.

docs_url.description: The vendor documentation the pack follows.

match.description: Which mail the pack claims: every condition of all, and at least one of any. The pack with the most matching conditions claims the message.

split.description: Digest mail: every match of record starts a record, which runs to the next match or the end of the body.

status_rules.description: Tried in order on every record; the first that matches gives the status. None matching gives unknown.

fixtures.description: Sample mails: fixtures/<pack id>/<name>.eml with <name>.expected.json beside it.

class.description: The kind of mail: the status it reports, digest for several records, or unmatched for mail the pack must not parse.

regex.description: A pattern of the regex module (re syntax); flags inline, such as (?i) or (?m).

scope.description: Where a regex looks: the record (default; the whole body without split), the whole body, or a header.

field.description: regex: a pattern with exactly one named group, whose text is the value; or literal: a fixed value.

time_field.description: Like field; format is a strptime format, else ISO 8601 or RFC 2822 is read. A time without a zone takes the zone of the mail's Date header, else UTC.
